 MESSAGE FROM THE CEO
 I assume the responsibility of leading Ecopetrol at
a pivotal moment for the company. We are embarking on a new phase focused on strengthening business competitiveness, restoring market
confidence and executing a strategy aimed at sustainable value creation. To achieve this, we are building a high-level executive team
that will enable us to capture opportunities in exploration, production of oil and gas, and enhance the performance of our core businesses.
 Our commitment is clear: to manage capital with discipline,
maximize investment profitability and deliver competitive returns. We will work to strengthen free cash flow to support growth and dividends,
maintain healthy debt levels, foster an enduring culture of cost restraint, efficiency and discipline, and ensure timely, reliable and
transparent financial information.
 Operationally, we will focus on growing reserves through
value-focused barrels, strengthening exploration activities, and pursuing new growth opportunities in Colombia and abroad. At the same
time, we will support efforts to strengthen the country’s energy and natural gas supply security and reliability at competitive
prices, including advancing key offshore developments, while attracting investment, fostering strategic partnerships and revitalizing
the oil and gas industry under Ecopetrol’s leadership.
 We recognize the challenges in our operating environment:
geopolitical volatility, rising logistics and financing costs, and natural field decline, require disciplined execution, supported by
the strengths of our integrated model, the development of long-term growth projects, our competitive advantage in heavy crude marketing,
and close coordination with the National Government to restore the country’s energy sovereignty.
 Our commitment is to translate this vision into tangible
results. We will act with financial discipline, operational excellence and rigorous capital allocation to strengthen Ecopetrol’s
competitiveness, restore market confidence and create value for all our shareholders.
 Joaquín Gutiérrez 
Ecopetrol S.A. CEO

 Highlights 
 | · | Financial Results: In
3Q26, the pricing environment was a key driver of results, helping offset operating pressures arising from lower production and scheduled
maintenance at Barrancabermeja Refinery. During the first nine months of the year, Ecopetrol improved its net income by 83% compared to
the same period of 2025, driven primarily by a favorable pricing environment that, together with higher refinery throughput, helped offset
a higher tax burden (wealth tax and the higher corporate income tax surcharge (15%)) and a lower exchange rate. | · | Brava Acquisition: 
In August 2026, Ecopetrol completed the acquisition of 51% of Brava Energía, beginning its financial consolidation into Ecopetrol
Group’s results in September. In its first month of consolidation, Brava contributed COP 0.6 trillion to EBITDA and COP 0.1 trillion
to net income. | · | Production: In 3Q26 total
production was 747 mboed. The consolidation of Brava strengthened the Ecopetrol Group’s production during 3Q26, offsetting the effects
of lower United States production, Colombian natural field decline and water-handling constraints in the Llanos region. | · | Cash Flow: At the end
of 3Q26, Ecopetrol Group’s consolidated cash totaled COP 16.3 trillion, including COP 3.1 trillion contributed by Brava. | · | Investment: In 9M26, Ecopetrol
Group made organic investments of USD 4,766 million (COP 16.7 trillion); 65% was deployed in Colombia and the remaining 35% in international
operations. | 
 Inorganic investments amounted to USD 1.4
billion, including the acquisition of Brava in Brazil (USD 1.2 billion), the acquisition of the Madeira stake in ISA Brasil (USD 0.2 billion),
and the entry payment associated with an Ecopetrol renewable energy project.

 Sales
Revenue
 Sales revenue
in 3Q26 totaled COP 35.1 trillion, up +17.5%, equivalent to COP +5.2 trillion compared to 3Q25, reflecting the net effect of:
 | · | Sales of crude oil, gas and refined products, before including
Brava Energía, increased by COP +4.5 trillion, mainly due to the favorable effect of the weighted-average selling price of the
sales basket, which reached 105.6 USD/bl, up +36.0 USD/bl from the comparable period. This generated a positive impact of COP +11.4 trillion,
in line with higher Brent prices and historically high refined product margins, offsetting weaker negotiated crude oil differentials.
This effect was partially offset by a lower average exchange rate (COP -5.9 trillion) and lower sales volumes (-55.5 mboed), equivalent
to COP -1 trillion, associated with lower production. | · | The consolidation of Brava Energía’s
September results, which contributed COP +1.1 trillion to the Ecopetrol Group’s revenue. | · | A decline in service revenue
(COP -0.4 trillion), mainly due to a lower impact from contractual indexation factors on energy tariffs at ISA Brasil. | 
 Sales revenue for the nine months ended September totaled
COP 103.9 trillion, up +14.3%, equivalent to COP +13.0 trillion compared to the same period of the previous year, reflecting the net effect
of: i) higher sales of crude oil, gas and refined products excluding Brava Energía (COP +11.2 trillion), mainly due to the price,
exchange rate and volume factors described for the quarter; ii) the inclusion of Brava Energía’s September revenue (COP +1.0
trillion); and iii) higher revenue from power transmission services and toll roads (COP +0.7 trillion), mainly due to progress on power
and toll road projects, the performance of toll road concessions and growth in telecommunications at ISA.

 Combined Crude Oil
and Refined Products Basket: In 3Q26, the average realized price increased by USD 36.7/bl (+49.8%) compared with 3Q25. The
basket achieved a premium of USD 19.0/bl to Brent in 3Q26, representing the highest Group-level premium recorded since 2015.
 Crude Oil: The
average realized crude oil basket price increased by USD 17.9/bl (+28.0%) versus 3Q25, reflecting: (i) a USD 23.1/bl (+33.9%) increase
in Brent prices; and (ii) a USD 5.2/bl deterioration in differentials, from -USD 3.9/bl in 3Q25 to -USD 9.1/bl in 3Q26. Market conditions
were characterized by a higher geopolitical risk premium associated with tensions in the Middle East and concerns regarding the security
of export flows from the Gulf region, increased availability of Venezuelan and Canadian crude grades in key markets, and materially higher
freight costs, resulting in greater pressure on tanker availability and reduced logistical flexibility.
 Refined Products: 
In 3Q26, the refined products basket price increased by USD 52.5/bl versus 3Q25, driven by stronger market benchmarks relative to Brent,
particularly for middle distillates (diesel and jet fuel) and gasoline. This reflected lower global supply associated with supply disruptions
caused by the conflict in the Middle East, declining global inventories, and attacks on and shutdowns of refineries in Russia.
 Natural Gas: 
In 3Q26, the gas selling price increased from 28.8 USD/bl to 41.8 USD/bl (+45.2%), reflecting a tighter supply-demand balance and higher
firm contracting requirements. The commercial strategy implemented during the period enhanced pricing flexibility through more frequent
negotiations and a broader mix of contractual arrangements.
 5 | Cost
of Sales
 Cost of sales increased by +5.4%, equivalent to COP
+1.1 trillion, in 3Q26 compared to 3Q25, reflecting the net effect of:
 | · | Higher purchase costs for crude
oil and refined products, associated with higher international benchmark prices (COP +3.7 trillion). | · | Higher purchase volumes, amounting
to COP +1.0 trillion, mainly due to: i) higher fuel imports (COP +0.6 trillion, +19.4 mboed) to meet domestic demand during major maintenance
at Barrancabermeja Refinery; and ii) increased crude oil purchases and sales with third parties (COP +0.5 trillion, +19.6 mboed). | · | The inclusion of Brava Energía’s
September cost of sales of COP + 0.5 trillion. | · | An increase in operating and
other costs (COP +0.1 trillion), mainly due to the inflationary impact on rates and services, partially offset by efficiencies captured
during the period. | · | These effects were offset by
the positive impact of a lower average exchange rate on foreign currency costs (COP -3.1 trillion). | · | Inventory movements (COP -1.1
trillion) due to lower crude oil deliveries and the buildup of refined product inventories to meet future commercial commitments. | 
 Cost of sales for the nine months ending September
totaled COP 62.5 trillion, up +1.3%, equivalent to COP +0.8 trillion compared to the same period of the previous year. This change was
primarily explained by higher purchase prices for crude oil and refined products (COP +7.1 trillion), the consolidation of Brava’s
costs (+COP 0.5 trillion) and increased operating and other costs (COP +0.2 trillion), in line with the factors described for the quarter.
These impacts were largely offset by the favorable effect of the lower exchange rate on foreign currency costs (COP -7.0 trillion).
 Operating
and Exploration Expenses
 Operating and exploration expenses in 3Q26 increased
by +17.5%, equivalent to COP +0.5 trillion compared to 3Q25, mainly due to: i) recognition of the wealth tax of COP +0.3 trillion; ii)
fuel losses of COP +0.2 trillion; and iii) the effect of consolidating Brava’s expenses of COP +0.1 trillion. These effects were
partially offset by the business combination gain associated with ISA’s acquisition of Madeira of COP -0.1 trillion.
 For the nine-month period, operating and exploration
expenses increased by 15.4%, equivalent to COP +1.2 trillion, compared to the same period of 2025, mainly due to: i) recognition of the
wealth tax of COP +0.9 trillion; ii) higher expenses associated with fuel losses and repairs to transportation infrastructure of COP +0.4
trillion; iii) increased exploration activity, with asset write-offs of COP +0.3 trillion; and iv) the effect of consolidating Brava of
COP +0.1 trillion. These effects were partially offset by lower taxes, mainly those associated with the state of internal disturbance
measures applicable in 2025, of COP -0.3 trillion, and by the business combination gain associated with ISA’s acquisition of Madeira
and other effects of COP -0.2 trillion.
 Financial
Result (Non-Operating)
 The non-operating financial result in 3Q26 remained
at levels similar to 3Q25, mainly reflecting the net effect of the inclusion of Brava’s finance costs of COP +0.2 trillion, offset
by lower interest expense on foreign currency debt of COP -0.2 trillion, supported by a lower exchange rate against the U.S. dollar.
 For the nine-month period, the net non-operating financial
result decreased by 1.5%, equivalent to COP -0.1 trillion compared to the same period of 2025, mainly reflecting the net effect of:
 · | Higher foreign exchange
income of COP -0.5 trillion, given the combined effect of Ecopetrol Group’s net liability position in U.S. dollars and the appreciation
of the peso against the U.S. dollar. | 
 6 | · | Lower interest expense
on foreign currency debt of COP -0.5 trillion, mainly due to the lower exchange rate against the U.S. dollar. | 
 · | Recognition of the
financing cost associated with a structured liquidity management transaction executed in January 2026, involving the sale of economic
rights to VAT credit balances, of COP +0.5 trillion. | 
 · | Lower income from
investment portfolio valuation and other items of COP +0.3 trillion. | 
 · | Consolidation of
Brava’s finance costs of COP +0.2 trillion. | 
 Income
Tax
 In 3Q26, the effective tax rate reached 37.7%, compared
to 31.2% in 3Q25, and stood at 37.3% for 9M26, compared to 32.1% in 9M25. The increase was mainly due to recognition of the wealth tax,
which is not deductible for income tax purposes, and the higher income tax surtax applicable to Ecopetrol S.A. and Hocol S.A., which rose
from 0% in 2025 to 15% in 2026, based on the projected year-end Brent price. These effects were partially offset by stronger results at
companies operating under special tax regimes, such as Cartagena Refinery.
 Statement
of Financial Position
 Assets increased by 10.9% in 3Q26, an increase
of COP+31.1 trillion compared to June, mainly due to the inclusion of Brava (COP +27.5 trillion), ISA’s investments associated with
the acquisition of the remaining 49% interest in Madeira and in Chile the Ruta de los Lagos project (COP +5.6 trillion), higher FEPC accruals,
net of payments, due to the pricing environment (COP +3.5 trillion), and higher cash generation (COP +1.9 trillion). This growth was partially
offset by the effect of the lower closing TRM on subsidiaries’ U.S. dollar-denominated assets (COP -3.0 trillion) and by tax offsets
and other items (COP -4.4 trillion).
 Liabilities increased by 13.6% in 3Q26, an increase
of COP +23.7 trillion compared to June, mainly due to the inclusion of Brava (COP +19.8 trillion), recognition of liabilities at ISA associated
with the acquisition of the interest in Madeira and the Ruta de los Lagos project (COP +4.7 trillion), and additional debt incurred by
the Ecopetrol Group (COP +5.5 trillion), mainly to finance the acquisition of Brava and new debt at ISA. These increases were partially
offset by the effect of the lower closing TRM on foreign currency debt (COP -3.3 trillion), tax offsets during the period and other items
(COP -3.0 trillion).
 Equity at the end of 3Q26 was COP +117.0 trillion,
an increase of COP +7.4 trillion compared to June, mainly due to net income generated during the quarter and recognition of the 49% non-controlling
interest in Brava following its acquisition, offset by the effect of translating the assets and liabilities of subsidiaries whose functional
currency is USD. Ecopetrol shareholders accounted for 75% of share in equity and non-controlling interests for the remaining 25%.
 Update on the
customs adjustment proceedings initiated by DIAN concerning VAT on fuel imports
 To date, Ecopetrol and Refinería de Cartagena
have filed two and six actions, respectively, seeking annulment and restoration of rights against DIAN before the Administrative Courts
of Cundinamarca and Bolívar in connection with VAT claims on fuel imports. Litigation has progressed through the procedural stages,
and 7 of the 8 cases have been admitted by the respective courts.
 In addition, on October 13, 2026, DIAN issued Ruling
No. 100202208-1829, partially reconsidering its previous interpretation and confirming that VAT incurred on imports of tangible goods
is a tax matter and, therefore, if the taxpayer files an action for annulment and restoration of rights, the tax authority may not pursue
enforced collection against the taxpayer or impose precautionary measures, such as asset seizures.
 7 | Consequently, until the courts issue final decisions
on the relief sought in the actions brought by Ecopetrol and Refinería de Cartagena, the disputed amounts (VAT, penalties and interest)
are not enforceable, and DIAN may not collect them. Both seizures of the plaintiff Companies’ assets and offsets of the disputed
amounts against their tax credit balances would therefore be precluded while the dispute remains before the courts.
 Acquisition
of Brava Energia S.A.
 On August 17, 2026, Ecopetrol Group completed the acquisition
of a controlling 51% interest in Brava Energía for total consideration of USD 1,123 million. The acquisition was carried out through
two transactions: a voluntary tender offer for approximately 25% of the shares and the purchase of an additional interest of approximately
26% from significant shareholders, pursuant to the agreement signed on April 23, 2026.
 For purposes of consolidating results, 100% of its
revenue, costs and expenses are included beginning in September, with the portion of earnings attributable to non-controlling interests
recognized separately. In the statement of financial position, Brava’s assets and liabilities are consolidated line by line at 100%,
with the corresponding 49% non-controlling interest recognized in equity.
 Brava’s results are included in the Ecopetrol
Group’s Exploration, Development and Production segment, in line with the strategic and operating nature of the acquisition, its
integration into the business management model and the applicable IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) segment reporting
criteria.
 On August 5, 2026, Ecopetrol Capital AG secured a short-term
credit facility, under which USD 1.2 billion was drawn. The proceeds were subsequently provided through an intercompany loan to Ecopetrol
Investimentos do Brasil Ltda. to fund the acquisition of a 51% equity interest in Brava Energia. The main effects of consolidating Brava
are described below:
 Income statement: 
Brava’s consolidation in 3Q26 includes one month of operations, corresponding to September, with 100% of its results included, comprising
revenue of COP 1.1 trillion, generated mainly by crude oil sales in Brazil and exports, EBITDA of COP 0.6 trillion and a contribution
to net income of COP 0.1 trillion.
 Statement of financial
position: The consolidation of Brava resulted in the inclusion of assets of COP 27.5 trillion and liabilities of COP 19.8 trillion,
as well as a non-controlling interest of COP 3.7 trillion. These amounts are provisional and may be adjusted upon completion of the valuation
of the assets acquired and liabilities assumed.
 This transaction marks a milestone in our portfolio
growth and diversification strategy, through which we expect to strengthen the Ecopetrol Group’s presence in Brazil and add a significant
reserve and production base to support sustainable long-term value creation. In addition, the integration process is expected to leverage
complementary capabilities to accelerate reserve additions, improve operating efficiency and maximize asset performance.
 Following the acquisition closing, the integration
process began, encompassing a range of short-, medium- and long-term strategic and operating activities centered on the transfer of best
practices. In addition to the developments mentioned above, during the quarter we progressed with our analysis of reserve certification
supported by robust estimation, control and reporting processes under SEC criteria, as well as support for the development of a reserve
progression and project maturation plan. We also advanced initiatives aimed at cost optimization and alignment around a long-term sustainability
vision to help strengthen Brava’s operations and value creation.

 Cash Flow 
 At the end of 3Q26, Ecopetrol Group’s consolidated
cash totaled COP 16.3 trillion, including COP 3.1 trillion contributed by Brava. Liquidity during the quarter was primarily supported
by operating cash generation, collection of FEPC balances for 3Q25 and 4Q25, and higher financing. These resources helped to fund a portion
of the acquisition of Brava, Ecopetrol Group CapEx execution, ISA’s acquisition of 100% of Madeira and debt interest payments.
 Debt 
 Debt outstanding at the end of September 2026 was COP
119.5 trillion (COP +14.6 trillion compared to June 2026), equivalent to USD 36,076 million, of which USD 10,601 million corresponds to
ISA. The variation was mainly due to:
 - | The inclusion of
Brava Energía’s debt (COP +12.3 trillion). | 
 - | Debt raised from
international banks to finance the acquisition of Brava, amounting to USD 1,173 million (valued on September 30, 2026, in COP +3.9 trillion). | 
 - | New debt at Ecopetrol
Group companies (COP +1.7 trillion), mainly at ISA for developing its own projects. | 
 These effects were partially offset by the translation
of foreign currency financial obligations at the closing exchange rate (COP -3.3 trillion), recognized mainly in equity through hedge
accounting.
 The Ecopetrol Group’s Gross Debt/EBITDA ratio
was 2.1 times, below the upper limit set for 2026 (2.5 times). The Net Debt/EBITDA ratio was 1.9 times. The inclusion of Brava increased
the Gross Debt/EBITDA ratio by approximately 0.2 times, reflecting both the debt included through the acquisition and its associated EBITDA.

 Consolidated refinery throughput reached 411.8 mbd
during 3Q26, reflecting major maintenance at Barrancabermeja Refinery. Despite lower throughput compared to 2Q26 (438.6 mbd) and 3Q25
(428.7 mbd), value was captured through coordinated asset management and the exceptional margin environment during the quarter.
 The integrated gross refining margin reached 45.6 USD/bl,
a quarterly all-time high, exceeding the 2Q26 figure (29.8 USD/bl) by 53% and the 3Q25 figure (14.3 USD/bl) by 219%. This performance
was mainly supported by wider fuel differentials, particularly for diesel, jet fuel and gasoline, driven by supply constraints and international
geopolitical conditions.
 The main actions supporting these results were: i)
optimization of crude slates; ii) capture of favorable market differentials; iii) realization of synergies between Barrancabermeja and
Cartagena; iv) maximization of availability at Cartagena; v) operational management to mitigate the impacts of scheduled maintenance at
Barrancabermeja; and vi) implementation of operating, logistics, energy and commercial efficiency initiatives.

 During 3Q26, commercial management responded
effectively to a highly volatile environment, coordinating actions to ensure supply and operational continuity, diversifying markets,
customers and destinations, strengthening trading capabilities and expanding logistical optionality. Ecopetrol’s crude oils achieved
stronger price realizations relative to competing crudes, despite market volatility. In maritime logistics, Time Charter arrangements,
Contracts of Affreightment (COAs), and consecutive voyage agreements ensured operational continuity and generated mitigation efficiencies
amid high and volatile freight rates, which increased by 30% to 50%, depending on the type of vessel
 In terms of diversification, Ecopetrol strengthened
the presence of Castilla, Apiay, Vasconia, and Mares crude oils in the United States, China, India, Jamaica, and Africa. In addition,
Vasconia and Apiay crude oils were repositioned in Asian markets. Third-party trading operations generated a USD 1.4 million benefit in
3Q26, while the portfolio of traded crude oils was expanded to include the purchase and sale of Kutubu Blend.
 Furthermore, the first relet transactions,
involving the sale of chartering services to third parties, were completed. Ecopetrol also carried out the first receipt and transfer
of Castilla crude oil at the Panama Terminal Port (PTP), diversifying maritime routes to Asia and reducing transportation times.
 In the petrochemicals segment, the solid sulfur export
program was launched, with deliveries to Brazil, Peru, and Tanzania. The first exports of lubricant base oils to Chile and Lithuania were
also completed, and the Ecospirit 40 trademark was registered for a ten-year period.
